description: Use this when the user wants a weighted decision matrix, scored comparison, alternative ranking, or weight sensitivity analysis with explicit criteria, weights and scores. Accepts two to twenty options and one to eight criteria. Scores use a fixed zero-to-one-hundred scale; benefit means higher is better and cost means lower is better. Returns normalized weights, exact rankings and ties, pairwise break-even shares, up to four explicit weight scenarios and CSV. Does not research options, invent scores, infer preferences or predict outcomes.

criteria.description: Criteria in the same order as each option score array, e.g. [{"name":"Quality","weight":60,"direction":"benefit"},{"name":"Expense","weight":40,"direction":"cost"}].

direction.description: benefit favors higher scores; cost favors lower scores, e.g. cost for expense. Scores remain on the zero-to-one-hundred scale.

weight.description: Nonnegative importance weight, at most three decimal places, e.g. 60. Weights need not sum to one hundred.

name.description: Unique alternative name, e.g. Supplier A.

scores.description: One rating per criterion, in criterion order, e.g. [80,40]. Use comparable fixed-scale ratings, not raw mixed units.

items.description: A fixed-scale rating, with at most three decimal places, e.g. 80.

scenarios.description: Optional explicit weight scenarios, e.g. [{"label":"Cost emphasis","weights":[20,80]}].

weights.description: Replacement weights in criterion order, e.g. [20,80]. At least one must be positive.

name: calculate_decision_matrix
title: Calculate decision matrix
